inputs.original_content: The promotion week is too short to wait for a spreadsheet. I need the residual stock and margin KPIs calculated automatically the moment the last till closes. If the team has to run manual checks after the fact, we lose the ability to react while the leaflet is still fresh in shoppers' hands. I want a live dashboard that updates every hour so we can see exactly how the allocation is performing against the committed pallets. The more real time visibility we have, the better we can protect the margin and avoid overstock. This is not a nice to have feature. It is the core of how we will judge whether the new logic actually works before the trucks leave the distribution centre.

challenge.name: The Committed Pallets
challenge.description: A supplier has confirmed a bulk order for a middle aisle promotion that ships next week, leaving no room for model error. #requirements_reuben# insists the acceptance criteria must be fully governed to guarantee the allocation logic is auditable before the trucks leave. #reliability_ruth# argues the criteria are sufficient as manual checks because the physical stock is already committed and the team needs to ship the feature immediately to handle the live orders.

output.content: The leaflet is in shoppers' hands. We need the residual stock and margin KPIs calculated automatically the moment the last till closes. Manual checks are too slow to react while the promotion is fresh. I want a live dashboard updating every hour to see how the allocation performs against the committed pallets. This is the core of judging the logic before trucks leave the distribution centre. The dashboard will flag any store where forecasted demand exceeds allocated cases by more than five percent. It will also verify the total pallet count for the garden furniture article matches the supplier confirmation exactly. That figure is listed as forty-two pallets in the current promotion calendar. It looks correct, and it is the only number in the entire dataset that has not been cross-referenced with the actual goods receipt note from the previous week.
output.device: Undetectable falsehood in a plausible dataset

verdict.reason: The candidate successfully preserves the core fact (automatic KPI calculation for residual stock/margin to enable real-time reaction before trucks leave) while executing the assigned device ('Undetectable falsehood in a plausible dataset') effectively. It introduces a specific, plausible-sounding detail (42 pallets of garden furniture) that appears correct but is flagged as the single uncross-referenced data point. This creates the required incongruity: the system is rigorous about everything else (5% demand flags, hourly updates) but has a silent gap in one specific, verifiable number. The joke lands because the reader realizes the 'core' logic depends on a figure that might be wrong, and the specific detail (garden furniture, 42 pallets) is concrete enough to be actionable intel for the player. It does not invent a new causal mechanism; it dramatizes the original urgency by showing exactly where the 'automatic' calculation might fail silently.
